parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Word List

Detailed Meanings

😎
constrain[kənstrein]v.
To constrain something means to limit its development.
→ Jim cannot join us because he is constrained by previous plans.
😎
depot[di:pou]n.
A depot is a bus or train station.
→ He waited for his mother to arrive at the depot.
😎
emulate[emjuleit]v.
To emulate people means to imitate them because they are greatly admired.
→ As a small boy, he always tried to emulate his big brother.
😎
forefinger[fɔ:rfiŋgər]n.
The forefinger is the finger between one's thumb and middle finger.
→ He shouted, 'There it is!' and pointed with his forefinger.
😎
guts[gʌts]n.
The guts are all the organs inside a person or animal.
→ The doctor can tell you every process that happens in one's guts.
😎
inherent[inhiərənt]adj.
When something is inherent, it is a natural part of something else.
→ Sweating is an inherent bodily function when exercising.
😎
intimidate[intimideit]v.
To intimidate means to frighten others.
→ My dad intimidates my friends whenever they visit.
😎
janitor[dʒænitər]n.
A janitor is a person who makes repairs and takes care of a building.
→ The school janitor cleaned up the messy cafeteria.
😎
moist[mɔist]adj.
When something is moist, it is slightly wet.
→ The ground is still moist from the rain last night.
😎
nope[noup]adv.
Nope is an informal way of saying 'no'.
→ He asked if I had any money, and I had to say, 'Nope.'
😎
prod[prɔd]v.
To prod means to push someone or something with a finger or pointed object.
→ The bully prodded me in the chest with his finger.
😎
ransom[rænsəm]n.
A ransom is a sum of money paid to a kidnapper to set the person free.
→ He kidnapped the prince and demanded $1 million as ransom.
😎
restrain[ristrein]v.
To restrain someone or something means to use physical strength to stop them.
→ Mike restrained Allen from reaching the door.
😎
saliva[səlaivə]n.
Saliva is the watery liquid in people's mouths that helps in digestion.
→ The baby could not keep the saliva from dripping out of its mouth.
😎
spit[spit]v.
To spit means to force liquid from one's mouth.
→ He emerged from the pool and spit water from his mouth.
😎
sprint[sprint]v.
To sprint means to run very fast over a short distance.
→ The kids didn't want to be late to class, so they sprinted to the bus stop.
😎
stunt[stʌnt]n.
A stunt is something that is done in order to get attention or publicity.
→ The man jumped over the cars as a promotional stunt.
😎
tolerant[tɔlərənt]adj.
When people are tolerant, they are approved of because they accept others.
→ The tolerant leader thought that everyone was equal regardless of race.
😎
vampire[væmpaiər]n.
A vampire is a fictional monster that sleeps in a coffin and sucks people's blood.
→ The vampire snuck up on the woman and bit her in the neck.
😎
yawn[jɔ:n]v.
To yawn means to open one's mouth wide and breathe in air.
→ The child yawned and stretched her arms before bed for the night.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content:
I’m glad our teacher is so accepting of others as they are. [ 1 ]

Chewing gum creates a lot of watery liquid used for digestion and chewing food. [ 2 ]

She had to use physical strength to stop the big dog so that it did not try to attack us. [ 3 ]

Let’s see who can run fast over a short distance to the car in the shortest amount of time. [ 4 ]

Lots of people try to imitate the sports star. [ 5 ]

The ache is coming deep from within her organs within the body. [ 6 ]

Please take a slightly wet towel and wipe the surface of the table to clean it. [ 7 ]

She wore a ring on her finger between her thumb and middle finger. [ 8 ]

A lack of money might limit the development of the project. [ 9 ]

His answer is always an informal way of saying no. [ 10 ]
questions.explanation: tolerant (adj): accepting others.
saliva (n): watery liquid in the mouth.
restrain (v): to use physical strength to stop someone or something.
sprint (v): to run very fast over a short distance.
emulate (v): to imitate someone because they are admired.
guts (n): organs inside a person or animal.
moist (adj): slightly wet.
forefinger (n): the finger between thumb and middle finger.
constrain (v): to limit development.
nope (adv): informal way of saying no.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: After walking through the desert, the thirsty man had no saliva left in his mouth.
questions.explanation: saliva means watery liquid in the mouth.

questions.content: We’ve been waiting at the depot for two hours for the train to arrive!
questions.explanation: depot means a station.

questions.content: The joke was so funny that it made him yawn.
questions.explanation: yawn is opening mouth wide and breathing in air, usually due to tiredness, not from a joke.

questions.content: The tolerant coach didn’t think that girls were good enough to play on the team.
questions.explanation: tolerant means accepting others, contradicting the sentence.

questions.content: He spit on the ground to show his disgust for the situation.
questions.explanation: spit means to force liquid from one's mouth.

questions.content: I hope I don’t have to constrain another essay at school tomorrow.
questions.explanation: constrain means to limit development, incorrect context for writing an essay.

questions.content: The boy’s dream was to restrain as well as his father someday.
questions.explanation: restrain means to stop using physical strength, incorrect context.

questions.content: He is usually a very calm person. His anger today was just an inherent act.
questions.explanation: inherent means a natural part of something, contradicting 'usually a very calm person'.

questions.content: The evil man expected a large ransom before he would return the child to her mother.
questions.explanation: ransom is money paid to a kidnapper.

questions.content: The rotten meal gave me a terrible pain in my guts.
questions.explanation: guts means the organs inside a body.

questions.content: I intimidated my homework, so I could go outside and play baseball.
questions.explanation: intimidate means to frighten others, incorrect context.

questions.content: No one was impressed with Bobby’s stunt to get attention.
questions.explanation: stunt is something done to get attention.

questions.content: Using his forefinger, he pointed to a plane in the sky.
questions.explanation: forefinger is the pointing finger.

questions.content: Take plenty of water with you before you begin the journey across the moist desert.
questions.explanation: moist means slightly wet, deserts are typically dry.

questions.content: The janitor had to fix the heater before people could enter the building.
questions.explanation: janitor makes repairs and takes care of a building.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Kidnapping

Anne was a very quiet girl who had an inherent fear of almost everything. The kids at school would play tricks on her all the time. They would hide behind the door of the school janitor’s closet, then jump out to scare her. Once, a boy dressed up like a vampire and chased her down the street. Anne hated being constrained by her fears, but she didn’t know how to be brave.

She was walking home from school one day when someone came up behind her. Before she could turn around, a powerful man grabbed her. She couldn’t scream because a huge hand was put over her mouth. Anne knew that this could not be another stunt by her classmates. The scary man restrained her arms and legs and carried her to his house. He tied Anne to a chair. Her guts began to hurt because she was so scared.

The man prodded Anne with his forefinger and said, “You’ll stay right here until I get a ransom from your parents. Then I’ll be rich!” The dirty man spit when he talked. A string of saliva hung from his moist lips. Anne was terrified and intimidated by the horrible man. But she knew she had to escape somehow.

Eventually, the man yawned. Anne waited quietly until he fell asleep. As he slept, she carefully wiggled her arms and legs until the ropes became loose. She slipped out of the ropes and carefully opened the door. She sprinted to the bus depot and boarded a bus to the police station. She told the police what happened, and they arrested the kidnapper.

The kids at school were amazed. They asked her, “Weren’t you too scared to escape?”

She said, “Nope, I knew that I had to be brave and get out of there!”

The kids were very tolerant of Anne from then on. They even decided that they would emulate her bravery if they ever got into a tough situation.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: Anne was constrained by her inherent fears.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Trong đoạn 1 có viết: "Anne hated being constrained by her fears..." (Anne ghét bị gò bó bởi những nỗi sợ hãi của chính mình...).

questions.content: The vampire restrained her arms and legs and carried her to his house.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Đoạn 2 ghi rõ: "The scary man restrained her arms and legs and carried her to his house." Không phải là "vampire" (ma cà rồng) mà là "scary man" (người đàn ông đáng sợ) đã trói tay chân và mang cô về nhà hắn.

questions.content: Anne’s guts began to hurt because she was intimidated by her classmates.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Trong truyện viết: "Her guts began to hurt because she was so scared." (Ruột gan cô bắt đầu đau thắt lại vì quá sợ hãi) sau khi bị bắt cóc bởi kẻ xấu, chứ không phải vì bị đe dọa ("intimidated") bởi bạn cùng lớp.

questions.content: The dirty man spit when he talked.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Đoạn 3 có nhắc đến: "The dirty man spit when he talked. A string of saliva hung from his moist lips." (Gã đàn ông bẩn thỉu nhổ nước bọt khi hắn nói chuyện).

questions.content: At the end, the kids were tolerant of Anne and decided to emulate her bravery.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Ở đoạn cuối, tác giả có viết: "The kids were very tolerant of Anne from then on. They even decided that they would emulate her bravery..." (Bọn trẻ từ đó rất khoan dung với Anne. Chúng thậm chí quyết định sẽ noi gương lòng dũng cảm của cô...).

questions.content: What would the kids do in the janitor’s closet?
options: They would hide behind the door of the school janitor’s closet, and then jump out to scare her.
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 1 có ghi: "They would hide behind the door of the school janitor’s closet, then jump out to scare her." (Bọn trẻ sẽ trốn sau cánh cửa tủ đồ của người lao công ở trường, sau đó nhảy xổ ra để hù dọa cô bé). Vì vậy, đáp án đúng là A.

questions.content: What happened after the man yawned?
options: Anne waited quietly until he fell asleep.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 cho biết: "Eventually, the man yawned. Anne waited quietly until he fell asleep." (Cuối cùng, gã đàn ông ngáp. Anne lặng lẽ chờ đợi cho đến khi hắn ngủ thiếp đi). Do đó đáp án là A.

questions.content: After the man prodded Anne with his forefinger, what did he say about the ransom?
options: “You’ll stay right here until I get a ransom from your parents. Then I’ll be rich!”
“I forgot to ask for a ransom.”
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 3, sau khi chọc ngón trỏ vào Anne, hắn nói: "You’ll stay right here until I get a ransom from your parents. Then I’ll be rich!" (Mày sẽ ở ngay đây cho đến khi tao nhận được tiền chuộc từ bố mẹ mày. Khi đó tao sẽ giàu to!). Vậy đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: What did Anne do after she sprinted to the bus depot?
options: She boarded a bus to the police station. She told the police what happened, and they arrested the kidnapper.
She bought a ticket to another city.
questions.explanation: Cuối đoạn 4 có viết: "...She sprinted to the bus depot and boarded a bus to the police station. She told the police what happened..." (Cô bé chạy thục mạng đến bến xe buýt và lên xe đến đồn cảnh sát. Cô kể cho cảnh sát nghe chuyện gì đã xảy ra...). Đáp án A là hoàn toàn chính xác.

questions.content: To what question did Anne respond by saying “ nope” ?
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 5 và 6, bọn trẻ hỏi: "Weren’t you too scared to escape?" (Cậu không quá sợ hãi để trốn thoát sao?), và Anne trả lời: "Nope, I knew that I had to be brave..." (Không, tớ biết rằng mình phải can đảm...). Vậy câu hỏi mà Anne phản hồi "nope" chính là A.
